entries.name: control-long-long-v3-accept#0
entries.script: [A1] `1L + 2L` at tree v3 — THE CONTROL. 3L at cost 25; nothing to upcast, so v3 and v0 agree and the pair below is what isolates the Upcast.

entries.name: control-long-long-v0-accept#1
entries.script: [A2] `1L + 2L` at tree v0 — the control's v0 twin, also 3L at 25.

entries.name: long-plus-int-v3-errored#2
entries.script: [A3] `1L + 2` at tree v3 — from v3 the builder inserts NO Upcast, so ArithOp takes the LEFT operand's static type and casts both values to it and the Integer is cast to Long: ClassCastException. THE SEPARATING ROW of the pair.

entries.name: long-plus-int-v0-accept#3
entries.script: [A4] `1L + 2` at tree v0 — the builder inserts an Upcast over the Int (SigmaBuilder.scala:757-763): 3L at cost 35. Against A2's 25, the v0 twin returns, so the inserted Upcast's cost is the difference — Int -> Long is 10.

entries.name: long-plus-any-v3-errored#4
entries.script: [A5] `1L + ByIndex((1,2,3), 0)` at tree v3 — the right operand is SAny-typed, and applyUpcast only widens NUMERICS, so there is nothing to insert: throws.

entries.name: long-plus-any-v0-errored#5
entries.script: [A6] `1L + ByIndex((1,2,3), 0)` at tree v0 — throws at v0 TOO, which is what separates an SAny operand from a narrow numeric one: the version gate does not reach it.

entries.name: int-plus-long-v3-errored#6
entries.script: [B1] `2 + 1L` at tree v3 — the narrower operand on the LEFT. ArithOp takes the LEFT operand's static type and casts both values to it, so the LONG is cast DOWN: ClassCastException Long -> Integer. The exception's DIRECTION is the evidence for the rule, A3 failing the other way on the same pair of types.

entries.name: int-plus-long-v0-accept#7
entries.script: [B2] `2 + 1L` at tree v0 — 3L at cost 35, the same as A4: the Upcast goes on whichever side is narrower, so the cost does not depend on the order.

entries.name: bigint-plus-long-v3-errored#8
entries.script: [B3] `BigInt(1) + 2L` at tree v3 — throws, CCE Long -> sigma.BigInt.

entries.name: bigint-plus-long-v0-accept#9
entries.script: [B4] `BigInt(1) + 2L` at tree v0 — BigInt 3 at cost 60. Against C1's 30 the Upcast to BigInt costs 30, THREE TIMES the Int -> Long one: the inserted node's cost scales with the target width, so a flat-cost model is 20 short here.

entries.name: control-bigint-bigint-v3-accept#10
entries.script: [C1] `BigInt(1) + BigInt(2)` at tree v3 — THE BIGINT CONTROL, 30 at both versions. Without it B4's 60 would be read against the LONG base of 25 and the Upcast mis-costed at 35; the family exists to make that subtraction legitimate.

entries.name: control-bigint-bigint-v0-accept#11
entries.script: [C2] `BigInt(1) + BigInt(2)` at tree v0 — the control's v0 twin, also 30.

entries.name: if-false-long-int-v3-accept#12
entries.script: [B5] `If(false, 1L, 2)` alone at tree v3 — Int 2 at cost 20. `If.tpe` is the TRUE branch's (Long) and nothing checks the false one, so this is a Long-typed expression with an Int VALUE. The lever for B7-B10, and it must keep returning or they prove nothing.

entries.name: if-false-long-int-v0-accept#13
entries.script: [B6] `If(false, 1L, 2)` alone at tree v0 — Int 2 at 20, unchanged: the If is indifferent to the version, so B8/B10's throws are not the builder's doing.

entries.name: long-plus-narrow-value-v3-errored#14
entries.script: [B7] `1L + If(false, 1L, 2)` at tree v3 — both static types are already Long, so there is no Upcast to insert and the narrow VALUE is cast: throws.

entries.name: long-plus-narrow-value-v0-errored#15
entries.script: [B8] `1L + If(false, 1L, 2)` at tree v0 — throws at v0 TOO. THE ROW THE FAMILY IS FOR: the static types agree, so the version gate has nothing to do, and a value narrower than its static type fails at EVERY version.

entries.name: narrow-value-plus-int-v3-errored#16
entries.script: [B9] `If(false, 1L, 2) + 2` at tree v3 — the narrow value on the LEFT: the Long implementation is chosen from the static type and gets an Integer. Throws.

entries.name: narrow-value-plus-int-v0-errored#17
entries.script: [B10] `If(false, 1L, 2) + 2` at tree v0 — throws at v0 too, the mirror of B8 with the narrow value on the other side.
